sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Have you ever been frustrated with someone who never seems to change their behavior?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾对一个似乎永远不会改变行为的人感到沮丧？

sentences.en: You remind your partner, again, not to leave dirty dishes in the sink.
sentences.zh: 你再次提醒你的伴侣，不要把脏碗碟留在水槽里。

sentences.en: You've had this conversation before.
sentences.zh: 这样的对话你们已经进行过很多次了。

sentences.en: Maybe you snap at them.
sentences.zh: 也许你会对他们发火。

sentences.en: Maybe you roll your eyes and do it yourself.
sentences.zh: 也许你会翻个白眼，然后自己动手做了。

sentences.en: Or maybe you get frustrated and throw up your hands.
sentences.zh: 又或者，你感到沮丧，只能无奈地摊开双手。

sentences.en: Or maybe it's your child who melts down in the middle of the grocery store
sentences.zh: 又或者是你的孩子在杂货店中间大发脾气，

sentences.en: or a co-worker who fails to meet deadlines in spite of endless reminders.
sentences.zh: 或者是一个同事，尽管你不断提醒，却总是无法按时完成工作。

sentences.en: No matter how many times we bring it up or how many strategies we try,
sentences.zh: 无论我们提起多少次，或者尝试了多少种策略，

sentences.en: nothing gets them to change.
sentences.zh: 都无法让他们做出改变。

sentences.en: Before long, resentment sets in.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，怨恨就开始滋生。

sentences.en: The temptation is to push harder.
sentences.zh: 人们往往会倾向于施加更大的压力。

sentences.en: More reminders.
sentences.zh: 更多的提醒。

sentences.en: More rules.
sentences.zh: 更多的规则。

sentences.en: More consequences.
sentences.zh: 更多的惩罚。

sentences.en: We tell ourselves they must be stubborn, defiant, oppositional.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉自己，他们一定是很固执、叛逆或存心作对。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，

sentences.en: research that explains why the techniques we use to get people to change their behavior
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨为何我们用来改变他人行为的技巧

sentences.en: are often strikingly ineffective.
sentences.zh: 往往效果甚微。

sentences.en: And we look at better ways to help the people we care about make lasting change.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨帮助我们在乎的人实现持久改变的更好方法。

sentences.en: It can be frustrating when people do things we don't want them to.
sentences.zh: 当人们做出我们不希望他们做的事情时，这确实令人沮丧。

sentences.en: A friend cancels plans at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 朋友在最后一刻取消了计划。

sentences.en: A loud co-worker dominates every meeting.
sentences.zh: 吵闹的同事在每次会议上都喧宾夺主。

sentences.en: A child refuses to get dressed for school.
sentences.zh: 孩子拒绝穿上校服去上学。

sentences.en: What goes through our minds in those moments?
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，我们的脑海里在想些什么？

sentences.en: And how do our mindsets affect our ability to influence others to change?
sentences.zh: 我们的心态又是如何影响我们引导他人改变的能力的？

sentences.en: At Harvard Medical School,
sentences.zh: 在哈佛医学院，

sentences.en: psychologist Stuart Ablon studies the science of helping people change.
sentences.zh: 心理学家斯图尔特·阿布隆正在研究帮助人们改变的科学。

sentences.en: Stuart Ablon, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特·阿布隆，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: I appreciate you having me.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: Stuart, you first became interested in psychology during your senior year of high school.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特，你是在高中最后一年开始对心理学产生兴趣的。

sentences.en: You got a job working with kids.
sentences.zh: 当时你找了一份与孩子们一起工作的工作。

sentences.en: Tell me about the work you were doing.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你当时做的工作吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, in high school, one of my first, you know, more serious jobs
sentences.zh: 是的，在高中时，我最早的、你知道的，比较正式的工作之一，

sentences.en: was working on an inpatient psychiatry unit for kids and adolescents.
sentences.zh: 是在一家针对儿童和青少年的住院精神科病房工作。

sentences.en: So this is where kids and adolescents go when their behavior is really out of control
sentences.zh: 这里是那些行为严重失控的儿童和青少年去的地方，

sentences.en: and they are at risk of hurting themselves or someone else.
sentences.zh: 他们有伤害自己或他人的风险。

sentences.en: And they're usually admitted against their will.
sentences.zh: 而且他们通常是被强制入院的。

sentences.en: And I had an internship there, really.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我当时在那里实习。

sentences.en: And I had no idea what to expect.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I remember on my first day, I was supervising along with some other staff,
sentences.zh: 我记得第一天，我和其他一些工作人员一起监督，

sentences.en: kids out on the playground.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在操场上玩耍。

sentences.en: And this young man started to get upset, really frustrated and lose his cool.
sentences.zh: 有个年轻人开始变得不安，非常沮丧，失去了冷静。

sentences.en: And he could tell I was the new person.
sentences.zh: 他看得出我是个新人。

sentences.en: And he said all kinds of awful things to me and went to try to attack me, really.
sentences.zh: 他对我说了各种难听的话，真的试图攻击我。

sentences.en: And he spat in my face and he kicked me where you don't want to be kicked.
sentences.zh: 他朝我脸上吐口水，还踢了我不该被踢的地方。

sentences.en: And I was incredibly taken aback.
sentences.zh: 我当时被吓坏了。

sentences.en: And one of the sort of more senior staff members approached quickly to rescue me.
sentences.zh: 一位资深员工迅速走过来救我。

sentences.en: And he said, let me show you how this is done here.
sentences.zh: 他说，让我教教你这里是怎么处理的。

sentences.en: And he sort of grabbed this young man and wheeled him around and
sentences.zh: 他抓住了那个年轻人，把他转过来，

sentences.en: and wrapped his arm around him and sort of like what we call a physical hold, a restraint,
sentences.zh: 用手臂环抱住他，也就是我们所说的身体控制，一种约束，

sentences.en: so that he couldn't spit at him or he couldn't, you know, kick him and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这样他就不能吐口水，也不能踢人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And this was my first on-the-job training about how to perform a physical restraint.
sentences.zh: 这就是我关于如何进行身体约束的第一次在职培训。

sentences.en: I mean, you must have been 16 or 17 years old at the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你当时一定才16或17岁。

sentences.en: And the kid couldn't have been much younger than you.
sentences.zh: 那个孩子肯定比你大不了多少。

sentences.en: It's a very good point.
sentences.zh: 说得太对了。

sentences.en: I forget whether I was 17 or may have just turned 18.
sentences.zh: 我不记得当时是17岁还是刚满18岁。

sentences.en: But be honest, I'm actually getting goosebumps talking about it,
sentences.zh: 但老实说，谈到这件事我甚至还会起鸡皮疙瘩，

sentences.en: even though I've talked about it a lot, because it was awful.
sentences.zh: 尽管我已经谈过很多次了，因为它太可怕了。

sentences.en: So you head home that evening.
sentences.zh: 所以那天晚上你回家了。

sentences.en: The next day, I understand you run into this young man again.
sentences.zh: 第二天，我听说你又遇到了这个年轻人。

sentences.en: His name is Jason.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫杰森。

sentences.en: What happens to it?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么事？

sentences.en: I was particularly on guard as I passed by the room where Jason was and nervous.
sentences.zh: 我经过杰森的房间时特别警惕，也很紧张。

sentences.en: And he called out to me.
sentences.zh: 他叫住了我。

sentences.en: I remember I was trying to walk by pretty swiftly, actually,
sentences.zh: 我记得当时我其实正试图快速走过，

sentences.en: so I wouldn't have to engage with him for fear of what might happen.
sentences.zh: 因为害怕发生什么事，所以不想和他接触。

sentences.en: And he called my name and I sort of turned around and I looked at him and he looked at me.
sentences.zh: 他叫了我的名字，我转过身看着他，他也看着我。

sentences.en: And he said to me, hey, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 他对我说，嘿，对不起。

sentences.en: I'm sorry about what I said.
sentences.zh: 我为我说的话道歉。

sentences.en: I really didn't mean it.
sentences.zh: 我真的不是那个意思。

sentences.en: I just lose control like that.
sentences.zh: 我只是会那样失去控制。

sentences.en: And I don't even know what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道自己在说什么。

sentences.en: And I just looked at him and I said, okay, it's all right.
sentences.zh: 我看着他说，好吧，没关系。

sentences.en: I accept your apology.
sentences.zh: 我接受你的道歉。

sentences.en: It's okay.
sentences.zh: 没事的。

sentences.en: What went through your mind at that point, Stuart?
sentences.zh: 那时候你心里在想什么，斯图尔特？

sentences.en: Because in some ways, it was not just surprising,
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，这不仅令人惊讶，

sentences.en: but I think in some ways it was also revelatory what happened in that moment.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在某种程度上，那一刻发生的事情也具有启示意义。

sentences.en: Yeah, what went through my mind again, I mean, just retelling this, Shankar,
sentences.zh: 是的，我心里在想什么，我的意思是，再次重述这件事，尚卡尔，

sentences.en: I'm emotional just retelling it because, you know, this kid I had this horrific interaction with
sentences.zh: 我重述时都很激动，因为你知道，这个孩子我曾与他有过可怕的互动，

sentences.en: and he said these awful things to me and I was trying to avoid him as soon as I arrived.
sentences.zh: 他对我说了那些难听的话，我一到那里就试图避开他。

sentences.en: And he's apologized to me.
sentences.zh: 而他却向我道歉了。

sentences.en: Clearly, this kid deeply regretted his behavior.
sentences.zh: 显然，这个孩子对自己行为深感后悔。

sentences.en: And this was just one tiny instance.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个小小的例子。

sentences.en: I can only imagine what had gone on to get him to this inpatient psychiatry unit in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我只能想象他经历了什么才被送到这个住院精神科病房。

sentences.en: And here he is clearly feeling terribly about this behavior, which, as he's explaining to me, you know, he just can't control.
sentences.zh: 而他现在显然对这种行为感到非常难过，正如他向我解释的那样，他只是无法控制。

sentences.en: So you eventually become a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你最终成为了一名临床心理学家。

sentences.en: And some years later, you're interviewing another young man who is in a correctional facility.
sentences.zh: 几年后，你正在采访另一名在惩教所的年轻人。

sentences.en: Tell me the story.
sentences.zh: 讲讲这个故事吧。

sentences.en: What was he in for?
sentences.zh: 他因为什么被关进去的？

sentences.en: So this young man was in for attempted murder.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人是因为谋杀未遂被关进去的。

sentences.en: He had shot someone.
sentences.zh: 他开枪打伤了人。

sentences.en: And, you know, I had next to no experience working in correctional facilities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我几乎没有在惩教所工作的经验。

sentences.en: So it's sort of, frankly, while I had the credentials at that point, it felt pretty similar to that interaction with Jason.
sentences.zh: 所以坦白说，虽然那时我已经有了资历，但感觉和与杰森的那次互动非常相似。

sentences.en: And I remember sitting very close across a bench from him.
sentences.zh: 我记得我坐在长凳上，离他很近。

sentences.en: So our faces were pretty close to each other.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的脸离得很近。

sentences.en: And I asked him, I said, you know, if you don't mind, would you mind telling me, like, what you were thinking when you did this?
sentences.zh: 我问他，我说，如果你不介意的话，能告诉我你做这件事的时候在想什么吗？

sentences.en: And I'll never forget this because he leaned in real close to me.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记这一点，因为他凑得非常近。

sentences.en: And he said to me, that is the stupidest question anybody's ever asked me.
sentences.zh: 他对我说，这是我听过最愚蠢的问题。

sentences.en: And one thing I can say about myself is I don't tend to be particularly defensive.
sentences.zh: 关于我自己，有一点我可以肯定，我通常不会特别有防御心理。

sentences.en: So I said to him, you know, that might be right.
sentences.zh: 所以我对他说，你知道，也许你是对的。

sentences.en: That might be the stupidest question anybody's ever asked you.
sentences.zh: 那可能是别人问过你最愚蠢的问题。

sentences.en: But do you mind telling me why that's such a stupid question?
sentences.zh: 但你介意告诉我为什么这是一个愚蠢的问题吗？

sentences.en: And he looked at me and he leaned in even closer and he said, do you think if I was thinking I would have done that, you moron?
sentences.zh: 他看着我，凑得更近了，他说，你以为如果我在思考，我还会做那种事吗，你这个白痴？

sentences.en: And I remember thinking to myself, God, yeah, of course, that is the stupidest questions anybody's ever asked.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时心想，天哪，是的，当然，这是别人问过最愚蠢的问题。

sentences.en: Because why would he do this if he were thinking?
sentences.zh: 因为如果他在思考，他为什么要这样做呢？

sentences.en: To me, that was an important moment.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是一个重要的时刻。

sentences.en: And reminded me, honestly, of, you know, in graduate school, we learned about aggressive responses and the difference between proactive aggression and reactive aggression.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这让我想起了在研究生院学到的关于攻击性反应，以及主动攻击和被动攻击之间的区别。

sentences.en: And most people think that horribly aggressive acts are like planned acts where the vast majority of them are poor responses to frustration and not thinking things through.
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为可怕的攻击行为是预谋的，而绝大多数其实是对挫折的拙劣反应，并没有经过深思熟虑。

sentences.en: You know, many years ago, I remember speaking with some researchers who are doing work in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 你知道，多年前，我记得与一些在芝加哥工作的研究人员交谈过。

sentences.en: And there was this sociologist, Harold Pollack, at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 当时芝加哥大学有一位社会学家，哈罗德·波拉克。

sentences.en: He looked through all the homicide cases that he could find in the city and then looked at what led to the homicide.
sentences.zh: 他查阅了该市所有他能找到的凶杀案，然后研究了导致凶杀的原因。

sentences.en: And again, his belief was that homicides happened because of premeditated gang violence.
sentences.zh: 同样，他原本认为凶杀案是由于预谋的帮派暴力引起的。

sentences.en: But what he found was very much what you're talking about, Stuart, which is there were interactions that went wrong.
sentences.zh: 但他发现的情况和你说的非常相似，斯图尔特，那就是互动出了问题。

sentences.en: People lost their tempers.
sentences.zh: 人们失去了理智。

sentences.en: Things escalated.
sentences.zh: 事情升级了。

sentences.en: Someone had access to a gun and someone got shot.
sentences.zh: 有人拿到了枪，有人被射杀了。

sentences.en: And over and over, what he found was that if people could pause, take a deep breath and count to 10,
sentences.zh: 他反复发现，如果人们能暂停一下，深呼吸并数到10，

sentences.en: it could mean the difference between a regular life and spending the rest of your life in prison.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着正常生活与余生在监狱中度过之间的区别。

sentences.en: Yes, that's impulse control.
sentences.zh: 是的，那就是冲动控制。

sentences.en: Literally, the definition of impulse control is taking a few seconds to think about the likely consequences of your actions before you act.
sentences.zh: 从字面上看，冲动控制的定义就是在行动之前花几秒钟思考一下你行为可能带来的后果。

sentences.en: And I always tell people, you know, if we didn't have that, we humans, if we didn't have impulse control, if we just did the first thing that came to our mind,
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉人们，你知道，如果我们没有这个能力，我们人类，如果我们没有冲动控制，如果我们只是做了脑海中浮现的第一件事，

sentences.en: said the first thing that came to our mind, the world would be an ugly place.
sentences.zh: 说了脑海中浮现的第一句话，这个世界将是一个丑陋的地方。

sentences.en: I usually tell people, if you want to do a little experiment,
sentences.zh: 我通常告诉人们，如果你想做一个小实验，

sentences.en: go through a day where you imagine you did or said the first thing that came to your mind throughout the course of the day.
sentences.zh: 试着过一天，想象你整天都做了或说了脑海中浮现的第一件事。

sentences.en: You'll amuse yourself, but you'll also be horrified about what the world would be like.
sentences.zh: 你会自娱自乐，但也会对这个世界会变成什么样感到恐惧。

sentences.en: When people do bad things, we often think it's because they're bad people, or they're being stubborn, or they're simply not trying hard enough.
sentences.zh: 当人们做坏事时，我们通常认为是因为他们是坏人，或者他们很固执，或者他们只是不够努力。

sentences.en: We attempt to help them fix this behavior through rewards and punishments, or we just encourage them to try harder.
sentences.zh: 我们试图通过奖惩来帮助他们纠正这种行为，或者只是鼓励他们更加努力。

sentences.en: When we come back, a psychological insight into a better way.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将深入探讨一种更好的心理学见解。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: It's easy to believe that our behavior is a matter of incentives.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易认为我们的行为取决于激励机制。

sentences.en: If I want to be healthy, I'll get some exercise.
sentences.zh: 如果我想保持健康，我会去锻炼。

sentences.en: If I want to get more done at work or school, I'll stop playing video games or watching so much TV.
sentences.zh: 如果我想在工作或学习中取得更多成就，我会停止玩电子游戏或看那么多电视。

sentences.en: When people act in certain ways or misbehave in certain ways, we feel it's because those are choices they're making.
sentences.zh: 当人们以某种方式行事或以某种方式表现不佳时，我们觉得这是因为他们做出了选择。

sentences.en: At Harvard Medical School, psychologist Stuart Ablon has tested the veracity of this belief.
sentences.zh: 在哈佛医学院，心理学家斯图尔特·阿布隆验证了这一信念的真实性。

sentences.en: Stuart, early in your career, you began working with a psychologist, Ross Green.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特，在你职业生涯早期，你开始与心理学家罗斯·格林合作。

sentences.en: He was developing a new approach to treating children with behavior probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在开发一种治疗儿童行为问题的新方法。

sentences.en: Tell me a little bit about what you did together.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你们一起做了些什么。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I had the good fortune of coming for my postdoctoral fellowship at Mass General Hospital in the Department of Psychiatry there,
sentences.zh: 我有幸来到麻省总医院精神科进行博士后研究，

sentences.en: and he was just getting started there as well.
sentences.zh: 他当时也刚在那里开始工作。

sentences.en: And he was my clinical supervisor for a year or so, and then we went on to work together for about 10 years.
sentences.zh: 他担任我的临床导师大约一年左右，之后我们一起工作了大约10年。

sentences.en: And what he was writing about as he was writing this book, The Explosive Child,
sentences.zh: 他在撰写《爆炸性儿童》这本书时，所探讨的核心内容是，

sentences.en: is decades of research that had shown that kids with very challenging, explosive behavior,
sentences.zh: 几十年的研究表明，那些表现出极具挑战性、爆发性行为的孩子，

sentences.en: that they struggled in certain areas of what we call neurocognitive skill or thinking skills.
sentences.zh: 在所谓的神经认知技能或思维技能的某些方面存在困难。

sentences.en: And so he was putting these ideas out there that, the way I talk about it,
sentences.zh: 他提出了这些观点，用我的话来说，

sentences.en: is that these kids seem to lack skill rather than will,
sentences.zh: 这些孩子似乎是缺乏技能，而不是缺乏意愿，

sentences.en: which was a bit of a revelation when you think of how we tend to respond to challenging behavior,
sentences.zh: 当你想到我们通常如何应对挑战性行为时，这确实是一个启示，

sentences.en: because it all revolves around trying to motivate people to behave better,
sentences.zh: 因为我们总是围绕着如何激励人们表现得更好来展开，

sentences.en: safe in the assumption that the reason they're not behaving well is because they lack the motivation to do so.
sentences.zh: 并理所当然地认为他们表现不好是因为缺乏动力。

sentences.en: I want to drill down into this because I think this is such a pervasive belief,
sentences.zh: 我想深入探讨这一点，因为我认为这是一种根深蒂固的信念，

sentences.en: which is that when we're trying to change someone and they don't change,
sentences.zh: 即当我们试图改变某人而他们没有改变时，

sentences.en: almost automatically, the thought comes to our mind,
sentences.zh: 我们几乎会自动地产生一个想法，

sentences.en: this person knows what they need to do.
sentences.zh: 这个人知道他们需要做什么。

sentences.en: They know what's going to be good for them to do.
sentences.zh: 他们知道怎么做对他们有好处。

sentences.en: They've agreed that it's the good thing for them to do,
sentences.zh: 他们也同意这样做是好事，

sentences.en: and they're not doing it.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是不做。

sentences.en: Clearly, it's a lack of will.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是缺乏意愿。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think one of the main reasons, though,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为主要原因之一，

sentences.en: that that thought kicks in for us so quickly
sentences.zh: 我们之所以会这么快产生这种想法，

sentences.en: is it's really aggravating when people don't do what we want them to do.
sentences.zh: 是因为当人们不按我们的意愿行事时，我们真的会很恼火。

sentences.en: So whether that's, you know, our child, our partner, our colleague, you name it,
sentences.zh: 所以无论是我们的孩子、伴侣、同事，还是其他任何人，

sentences.en: we get frustrated.
sentences.zh: 我们都会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And when we're frustrated,
sentences.zh: 而当我们感到沮丧时，

sentences.en: we humans don't tend to have as good access to the smart part of our brain.
sentences.zh: 我们人类大脑中负责理智的部分往往无法正常运作。

sentences.en: And frankly, we sort of reach very quickly for power and control
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我们很快就会诉诸权力和控制，

sentences.en: to try to restabilize things.
sentences.zh: 试图让局势重新稳定下来。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think that's part of the reason.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为这就是部分原因。

sentences.en: We've sort of long believed this.
sentences.zh: 我们长期以来一直相信这一点。

sentences.en: There's sort of a conventional wisdom around this that, you know, motivation,
sentences.zh: 有一种传统的观念认为，你知道，动力，

sentences.en: that behavior is all about motivation.
sentences.zh: 行为完全取决于动力。

sentences.en: But then you layer on top when people don't do what we want them to do
sentences.zh: 但当你再加上一层，即当人们不按我们希望的那样做，

sentences.en: or do things we don't want them to do.
sentences.zh: 或者做了我们不希望他们做的事情时，

sentences.en: It frustrates us.
sentences.zh: 这会让我们感到沮丧。

sentences.en: It triggers us.
sentences.zh: 这会触发我们的情绪。

sentences.en: And that makes it hard for us to have an empathic understanding
sentences.zh: 这使得我们很难产生共情理解，

sentences.en: or even an accurate understanding about what might be getting in that person's way.
sentences.zh: 甚至很难准确理解到底是什么阻碍了那个人。

sentences.en: I'm also curious about the fact that I think when we reach for that very quick conclusion,
sentences.zh: 我也很好奇，我认为当我们得出那个非常迅速的结论时，

sentences.en: and I appreciate what you just said,
sentences.zh: 我很赞同你刚才所说的，

sentences.en: which is that we reach for the conclusion in some ways because we are upset,
sentences.zh: 即我们在某种程度上得出这个结论是因为我们心烦意乱，

sentences.en: we are frustrated,
sentences.zh: 我们感到沮丧，

sentences.en: and the conclusion in some ways helps us deal with our own frustration to say,
sentences.zh: 而这个结论在某种程度上帮助我们应对自己的沮丧，即说，

sentences.en: okay, this person is just not doing what they know is the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这个人只是没有做他们明知是正确的事情。

sentences.en: But of course, once we get into that mindset,
sentences.zh: 但当然，一旦我们陷入这种心态，

sentences.en: now we locate the problem entirely in the other person.
sentences.zh: 我们就把问题完全归咎于对方。

sentences.en: And in some ways, what we're doing is we're giving up our own capacity
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们这样做是放弃了自己，

sentences.en: to potentially help them because we're saying
sentences.zh: 放弃了潜在的帮助他们的能力，因为我们说，

sentences.en: it's no longer anything that we can do that would be helpful.
sentences.zh: 我们已经无能为力了。

sentences.en: The problem is entirely with this other person.
sentences.zh: 问题完全出在对方身上。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not about me.
sentences.zh: 这与我无关。

sentences.en: It's about them.
sentences.zh: 是他们的问题。

sentences.en: And that's where a lot of blame happens.
sentences.zh: 这就是很多指责产生的地方。

sentences.en: We sort of absolve ourselves, take ourselves off the hook,
sentences.zh: 我们某种程度上宽恕了自己，摆脱了责任，

sentences.en: and we just blame the other person.
sentences.zh: 然后只是指责对方。

sentences.en: And, you know, the other thing that you're bringing up for me here
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在这里提出的另一件事是，

sentences.en: is when you look at challenging behavior,
sentences.zh: 当你审视挑战性行为时，

sentences.en: you know, it doesn't ever happen out of the blue for no reason.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它从来不是无缘无故发生的。

sentences.en: People don't explode or implode for no reason.
sentences.zh: 人们不会无缘无故地爆发或崩溃。

sentences.en: There's something that happens.
sentences.zh: 一定发生了什么事。

sentences.en: There's some context.
sentences.zh: 一定有某种背景。

sentences.en: There's some situation.
sentences.zh: 一定有某种情况。

sentences.en: There's some trigger.
sentences.zh: 一定有某种诱因。

sentences.en: And often, it takes two to tango.
sentences.zh: 而且通常，一个巴掌拍不响。

sentences.en: It's what you're asking the person to do,
sentences.zh: 这取决于你要求对方做什么，

sentences.en: how you're asking the person to do it,
sentences.zh: 你要求对方怎么做，

sentences.en: in what way, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 以什么方式，等等。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's not just as simple as the other person's fault.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这不仅仅是对方的错那么简单。

sentences.en: But again, that can make us feel better.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这能让我们感觉好受些。

sentences.en: I want to talk about some of the skills that might lead to
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈一些可能导致，

sentences.en: people not being able to change in the way we would like them to change.
sentences.zh: 人们无法按照我们希望的方式改变的技能。

sentences.en: You sometimes work with children in your practice as a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 作为一名临床心理学家，你有时会与儿童一起工作。

sentences.en: You once had a teenage patient who was very hard to get him to open up.
sentences.zh: 你曾经有一位青少年患者，很难让他敞开心扉。

sentences.en: Anytime you would try to engage with him in conversation,
sentences.zh: 每当你试图与他交谈时，

sentences.en: he would say the same thing over and over again.
sentences.zh: 他总是反反复复说同样的话。

sentences.en: Tell me about this, Charles Stewart.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这件事吧，Charles Stewart。

sentences.en: So this young man, you know, whenever I would really ask him for information about something,
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人，你知道，每当我真的想问他一些信息时，

sentences.en: you know, for instance, there was something that happened at school, an incident,
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如学校里发生了一件事，一个事故，

sentences.en: and I wanted his, you know, perspective on it and get his side of the story.
sentences.zh: 我想听听他的看法，了解他的那一面故事。

sentences.en: And when I would say to him, so can you tell me, you know, what happened?
sentences.zh: 当我问他，你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: He would say, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 他会说，我不在乎。

sentences.en: Often before I even got a chance to finish my question.
sentences.zh: 通常在我还没来得及问完问题之前就说了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I would say, well, you know, I'm just sort of curious if you don't mind,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我会说，好吧，如果你不介意的话，我只是有点好奇，

sentences.en: because I want to hear your side of the story.
sentences.zh: 因为我想听听你的那一面故事。

sentences.en: So if you can, he'd stop, stop me in the middle.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能，他会停下来，在中间打断我。

sentences.en: I don't give a ****.
sentences.zh: 我才不在乎呢。

sentences.en: And I said, well, you know, you may not give a ****, but I sort of do.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你可能不在乎，但我有点在乎。

sentences.en: So I would love to just get your, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 所以我很想得到你的，我不在乎。

sentences.en: And it just occurred to me that, like, he was sort of heading this off at the pass very quickly.
sentences.zh: 我突然意识到，他是在非常迅速地阻止这一切。

sentences.en: And oftentimes I hadn't even finished my question,
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候我甚至还没问完问题，

sentences.en: much less could he possibly have any, have had any time to think about what I was asking him.
sentences.zh: 更不用说他可能有时间去思考我问他的问题了。

sentences.en: I actually just said that to him.
sentences.zh: 我实际上就是这样对他说的。

sentences.en: I said, you know, I just noticed you, you say, I don't care really quickly,
sentences.zh: 我说，我注意到你很快就说我不在乎，

sentences.en: like before you even have time to think.
sentences.zh: 就像在你还没来得及思考之前一样。

sentences.en: So can you do me a favor?
sentences.zh: 所以你能帮我个忙吗？

sentences.en: Like, can I ask you the question and I'm going to give you a chance to think.
sentences.zh: 我可以问你问题，然后我会给你机会思考。

sentences.en: And after you think about it for a while, if you really don't care, don't give a ****,
sentences.zh: 在你思考了一会儿之后，如果你真的不在乎，不在乎，

sentences.en: then tell me that, okay?
sentences.zh: 那再告诉我，好吗？

sentences.en: And I'll believe you, but give it a chance.
sentences.zh: 我会相信你的，但请给它一个机会。

sentences.en: And so I asked him the same question.
sentences.zh: 于是我问了他同样的问题。

sentences.en: And I said to myself in my head, count to like 45.
sentences.zh: 我在心里对自己说，数到45左右。

sentences.en: And so I waited, counted, and somewhere past 30 before 45,
sentences.zh: 所以我等了，数着，在超过30到45之间，

sentences.en: he started filling me in a little bit about what happened.
sentences.zh: 他开始向我透露一点发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I said to him, so wait a sec, you told me you didn't care before,
sentences.zh: 我对他说，等等，你刚才告诉我你不在乎，

sentences.en: but it sounds like actually maybe you do.
sentences.zh: 但听起来其实你可能是在乎的。

sentences.en: And he said, yeah, I just said that.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，我只是那么说而已。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, well, I've noticed you say that a lot.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，我注意到你经常这么说。

sentences.en: Why do you think you do that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你为什么会那样做？

sentences.en: And he's like, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不知道。

sentences.en: And I decided let's do the same thing again.
sentences.zh: 我决定我们再做一次同样的事情。

sentences.en: But we'll think about it for a sec.
sentences.zh: 但我们会思考一会儿。

sentences.en: Because if you really don't know, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你真的不知道，那也没关系。

sentences.en: We can try to figure it out together.
sentences.zh: 我们可以试着一起找出原因。

sentences.en: But think about why do you think when somebody asks you something,
sentences.zh: 但想一想，为什么当别人问你什么时，

sentences.en: you just say, I don't, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 你只是说，我不在乎。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you a minute.
sentences.zh: 我会给你一分钟时间。

sentences.en: And he says, well, nobody's going to wait long enough
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，没有人会等那么久，

sentences.en: until I've thought about things, until I know what I'm going to say.
sentences.zh: 直到我思考清楚，直到我知道我要说什么。

sentences.en: So, you know, I might as well just stop it now.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不如现在就停止。

sentences.en: So basically what he was doing with, I don't care, I don't give a s***,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上他用我不在乎，我才不在乎，

sentences.en: was basically saying, let's call this off now,
sentences.zh: 基本上是在说，让我们现在结束吧，

sentences.en: because it's going to take me a while to process this
sentences.zh: 因为我需要一段时间来处理这个问题，

sentences.en: and come up with my thought and articulate it in spoken language.
sentences.zh: 并得出我的想法，然后用口头语言表达出来。

sentences.en: So you say this is an example of how language and communication skills
sentences.zh: 所以你说这是一个语言和沟通技巧，

sentences.en: can influence behavior.
sentences.zh: 如何影响行为的例子。

sentences.en: Say more about this, Stuart.
sentences.zh: 多说说这个，Stuart。

sentences.en: Well, language and communication skills are just crucial.
sentences.zh: 嗯，语言和沟通技巧至关重要。

sentences.en: You know, I always tell people, think about a time
sentences.zh: 你知道，我总是告诉人们，回想一下，

sentences.en: when most kids are poorly behaved.
sentences.zh: 大多数孩子表现不好的时候。

sentences.en: You know, when they have a lot of meltdowns, throw a lot of fits,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当他们有很多崩溃、发脾气的时候，

sentences.en: and everybody says, oh, two or three, you know, the terrible twos, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，哦，两三岁，可怕的两岁，对吧？

sentences.en: And think about when kids are two.
sentences.zh: 想想孩子两岁的时候。

sentences.en: There's a bunch of things that they're really bad at.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多事情做得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And we don't get worried yet because, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们还不担心，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: they're not supposed to be good at those things.
sentences.zh: 他们本就不应该擅长这些事情。

sentences.en: But they are horribly inflexible.
sentences.zh: 但他们非常缺乏灵活性。

sentences.en: They can't tolerate frustration.
sentences.zh: 他们无法忍受挫折。

sentences.en: And they have terrible problem-solving skills.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的解决问题能力很差。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons they have terrible problem-solving skills
sentences.zh: 他们解决问题能力差的原因之一是，

sentences.en: is they're just learning how to communicate with words,
sentences.zh: 他们才刚刚学习如何用语言交流，

sentences.en: which is why you see them communicate in all kinds of other ways.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会看到他们用各种其他方式进行交流。

sentences.en: But as they get better at knowing what's bothering them,
sentences.zh: 但随着他们越来越擅长了解什么在困扰他们，

sentences.en: putting it into words, engaging in a back and forth
sentences.zh: 用语言表达出来，进行来回沟通，

sentences.en: to try to solve a problem, their behavior improves as well.
sentences.zh: 试图解决问题，他们的行为也会改善。

sentences.en: Now, the reality is with this young man, he was a lot older than two,
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，这个年轻人比两岁大得多，

sentences.en: but his language skills hadn't really caught up with the average kid his age.
sentences.zh: 但他的语言能力并没有真正赶上同龄的普通孩子。

sentences.en: You know, it can look lots of different ways.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这看起来有很多不同的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, it can look like a lot of swearing like this kid.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它可能看起来像这个孩子一样有很多脏话。

sentences.en: A lot of times it looks like kids or adults who are silent.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，它看起来像沉默的孩子或成年人。

sentences.en: You might ask them to do something.
sentences.zh: 你可能会要求他们做某事。

sentences.en: And they just sort of look at you quietly.
sentences.zh: 他们只是安静地看着你。

sentences.en: And this is where what we talked about earlier comes in,
sentences.zh: 这就是我们之前谈到的内容发挥作用的地方，

sentences.en: because that's when we jump to conclusions.
sentences.zh: 因为那正是我们妄下结论的时候。

sentences.en: And we have these biases.
sentences.zh: 我们会有这些偏见。

sentences.en: We think to ourselves, oh, they're refusing to respond.
sentences.zh: 我们心里会想，噢，他们拒绝回应。

sentences.en: Maybe we think they're being passive-aggressive.
sentences.zh: 也许我们认为他们是在消极怠工。

sentences.en: Maybe they're not being passive-aggressive.
sentences.zh: 也许他们并没有消极怠工。

sentences.en: Maybe they're just thinking.
sentences.zh: 也许他们只是在思考。

sentences.en: You know, we have a segment on the show called Your Questions Answered,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的节目里有一个环节叫“解答你的问题”，

sentences.en: where we ask our listeners to send in questions.
sentences.zh: 我们会邀请听众寄来问题。

sentences.en: And I remember a question that came in recently from this woman.
sentences.zh: 我记得最近有一位女士寄来的问题。

sentences.en: And she said, you know, I've been married, I think, for 50 years.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道，我想我已经结婚50年了。

sentences.en: And I feel like I'm in my golden years now with my husband.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在我和丈夫正处于黄金岁月。

sentences.en: But I feel like every time I start a conversation, he parries me.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉每次我开启一段对话，他都在回避我。

sentences.en: He basically blocks me.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在阻断我。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to engage in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 他不想参与对话。

sentences.en: Every time I bring up, you know,
sentences.zh: 每次我提起，你知道，

sentences.en: why is it that we're not having a good conversation?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能好好聊聊呢？

sentences.en: He blocks me off at the pass.
sentences.zh: 他总是把话头掐断。

sentences.en: He doesn't talk to me again.
sentences.zh: 他就不再跟我说话了。

sentences.en: And I feel like I'm being stonewalled.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己被拒之门外了。

sentences.en: You know, I've been stonewalled for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我被这种冷暴力对待已经很多很多年了。

sentences.en: And I feel like I don't have a good relationship anymore.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们之间已经没有良好的关系了。

sentences.en: And I don't know what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: But in some ways, of course, the specifics might be different.
sentences.zh: 当然，在某些方面，具体情况可能有所不同。

sentences.en: We don't know what's happening with that particular family.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道那个家庭具体发生了什么。

sentences.en: But I'm hearing echoes in some ways of the story you just told me
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，我听到了你刚才告诉我的故事的回响，

sentences.en: with somebody who might be decades younger.
sentences.zh: 那是关于一个可能比她年轻几十岁的人的故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is where I say to myself,
sentences.zh: 这就是我对自己说的话，

sentences.en: try not to jump to conclusions that are blaming.
sentences.zh: 尽量不要妄下指责性的结论。

sentences.en: And instead, think skill, not will.
sentences.zh: 相反，要考虑能力问题，而不是意愿问题。

sentences.en: Think, maybe this person has a hard time engaging in those conversations.
sentences.zh: 想想看，也许这个人很难参与到这些对话中来。

sentences.en: Maybe they're not stonewalling intentionally.
sentences.zh: 也许他们并不是故意要冷暴力。

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，另一种可能性是，也许他们对进行这些对话有一些合理的顾虑，

sentences.en: about having these conversations,
sentences.zh: 但他们不太擅长表达这些顾虑。

sentences.en: but they're not very good at expressing those concerns.
sentences.zh: 所以表现出来就是冷暴力。
