sentences.zh: 另一种会影响我们行为和应对情况方式的技能，

sentences.en: Another skill that can affect the way we behave and respond in situations
sentences.zh: 是我们的工作记忆。

sentences.en: is our working memory.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特，请描述一下你所说的工作记忆，以及它在这里起到了什么作用。

sentences.en: Describe what you mean by working memory and how it plays a role here, Stuart.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 工作记忆，你知道，它不像试图回忆你前几天午饭吃了什么，

sentences.en: Working memory, you know, it's not like trying to remember what you had for lunch,
sentences.zh: 或者类似的事情。

sentences.en: you know, a couple of days ago or things like that.
sentences.zh: 工作记忆是神经心理学家所说的“认知架子”，

sentences.en: Working memory is what neuropsychologists call the cognitive shelf,
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中有一个架子，我们可以把东西放在上面。

sentences.en: the shelf we have in our brain where we can put something up on that shelf.
sentences.zh: 我们还能看到它。

sentences.en: We can still see it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要的时候可以随时拿取。

sentences.en: We can grab it when we need it.
sentences.zh: 我们对工作记忆的依赖程度远超我们的想象。

sentences.en: And we are much more reliant on our working memory than we have any idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我总是告诉人们，就像我们现在这样进行对话，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, I always tell people just having a conversation like we are right now, right?
sentences.zh: 比如我在说话时，你希望做的是倾听并在心里思考，

sentences.en: Like as I'm talking, what you're hopefully doing is listening and thinking to yourself,
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于他说的这些，我是怎么想的？

sentences.en: hmm, what do I think about what he's saying?
sentences.zh: 所以你手里拿着一条信息，就是他在说什么？

sentences.en: So you're holding one piece of information is what is he saying?
sentences.zh: 另一条信息是，对于他说的这些，我有什么想法？

sentences.en: Another piece is what am I thinking about what he's saying?
sentences.zh: 然后希望你也在对自己说，

sentences.en: Then hopefully you're also saying to yourself,
sentences.zh: 我想知道我该如何回应他所说的话。

sentences.en: I wonder how I might respond to what he's saying.
sentences.zh: 如果你表现得最适应环境，你甚至会对自己说，

sentences.en: And if you're really behaving in the most adaptive way, you're even saying to yourself,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，基于我对他说的话的看法，他会如何回应我可能说的话。

sentences.en: and I wonder how he'll respond to what I might say based upon what I think about what he's saying.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我并没有停止说话。

sentences.en: And by the way, I haven't stopped talking at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以你脑子里装满了所有这些信息。

sentences.en: So you're holding all this information in your head.
sentences.zh: 你必须同时在脑子里保持所有这些文件处于打开状态。

sentences.en: And you have to keep all those files open in your head at one time.
sentences.zh: 我经常注意到自己这一点，你知道，我试图获取某样东西，然后我说，

sentences.en: I often notice this about myself, you know, I'm trying to get something and I say,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我需要获取这条信息。

sentences.en: okay, I need to get this piece of information.
sentences.zh: 而这条信息在另一边的那个文件里。

sentences.en: And this piece of information is in this other file over here.
sentences.zh: 所以我去找那个文件，但我意识到那里缺少了一些东西，

sentences.en: So I go to that file, but I realize there's something there that's missing
sentences.zh: 或者我需要其他东西才能获取那条信息。

sentences.en: or that I need something else in order to get that information.
sentences.zh: 现在我突然陷入了死胡同，越陷越深。

sentences.en: And now I'm suddenly three steps down the rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 我必须记住如何爬回我最初遇到的那个问题。

sentences.en: And I have to remember how to climb my way back to the problem I had in the first place.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是工作记忆。

sentences.en: And all of that is working memory.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，而且你在这里指出的另一点是，工作记忆与注意力、组织能力等其他技能密切相关，

sentences.en: It is, and what you're also pointing out here is that working memory is incredibly closely related to other skills
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当我们研究工作记忆时，我们经常把它和注意力技能归为一类，

sentences.en: that have to do with attention and organization.
sentences.zh: 因为它们是相辅相成的，它们都构成了我们保持条理的能力，

sentences.en: And this is why when we study working memory, we often sort of lump it together with attentional skills
sentences.zh: 这也是一种技能。

sentences.en: because those, they sort of go together and they all amount to our ability to stay organized as well,
sentences.zh: 对于其中一些技能，有一个高级的术语，我们称之为执行功能技能，

sentences.en: which is, again, a skill.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，可以把它看作是你大脑的CEO。

sentences.en: And the fancy term for some of these skills is what we call executive functioning skills,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们想让某人做一些复杂的事情时，比如我们想让一个孩子在课堂上努力学习，

sentences.en: the sort of CEO of your brain, if you will.
sentences.zh: 可能在进入课程内容之前，需要涉及一整套学习技能。

sentences.en: So when we want someone to do something complex, you know, we want a kid to work hard in a class and study,
sentences.zh: 你说对了。

sentences.en: for example, there might be a whole set of study skills that are involved
sentences.zh: 绝对正确。

sentences.en: before you can actually get to what the class is even about.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们把这些视为理所当然。

sentences.en: You got it.
sentences.zh: 我曾辅导过一个孩子，他的房间总是像许多其他孩子一样乱七八糟。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 他的父母很生气，会叫他去打扫房间。

sentences.en: And, you know, we take these things for granted.
sentences.zh: 你走进他的房间，地板上堆满了脏衣服。

sentences.en: A kid I worked with, his room was always a mess like many other kids.
sentences.zh: 那个地方看起来就像被炸弹炸过一样。

sentences.en: And his parents were furious and would tell him to go clean his room.
sentences.zh: 他会走到书桌上方，那里有一些架子，

sentences.en: And you'd go into his room and there'd be like heaps of laundry on the floor.
sentences.zh: 然后他会开始擦拭架子顶角上的动作人偶，而你知道，

sentences.en: The place was like, looked like a bomb hit it.
sentences.zh: 最有效率的做法是把所有的衣服都放进洗衣篮里。

sentences.en: And he would go up to the above his desk where he had some shelves.
sentences.zh: 只需要三秒钟。

sentences.en: And he would start like dusting his action figures on the top corner of the shelf where, you know,
sentences.zh: 整个地方看起来会好得多。

sentences.en: the biggest bang for your buck would be take all the laundry and put it in the laundry basket.
sentences.zh: 但这个孩子，你知道，他很难从大局出发进行组织，

sentences.en: Take it three seconds.
sentences.zh: 而那是一种技能。

sentences.en: It'll whole place will look a lot better.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈过去常给我讲一个故事，当时她好像是在上高中或大学。

sentences.en: But this kid that, you know, he had a hard time thinking big picture and organizing like that.
sentences.zh: 她在各门课上都遇到了真正的困难。

sentences.en: And that's a skill.
sentences.zh: 人们花了几个月的时间才意识到，发生在她身上的是她患上了近视。

sentences.en: My mom used to tell me the story when she was, I think, in either high school or college.
sentences.zh: 她根本看不清黑板上发生了什么。

sentences.en: And she was having real trouble in various classes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种我们需要的最实用的技能，即清晰视物的能力。

sentences.en: And it took actually several months for people to realize that what was happening was she was developing myopia.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，你所谈论的是它的心理学类比，也就是说，当我们不能做某事时，可能是因为我们根本做不到。

sentences.en: And she simply couldn't see what was happening on the board.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a very practical kind of skill that we need, the ability to see clearly.
sentences.zh: 用这个类比来说，如果你告诉一个看不见东西的人，比如，你知道，例如，当我戴隐形眼镜时，我就读不了非常小的字。

sentences.en: But in some ways, what you're talking about is the psychological analogy for that, which is that when we can't do something, it could be because we're simply not able to do it.
sentences.zh: 你可以给我世界上最好的激励，或者告诉我会有最严重的后果，

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 如果我不去读它，那也没用。

sentences.en: And to use that analogy, if you tell somebody who can't see something, like, you know, for instance, when I wear my contact lenses, I can't read very small print.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这反而会降低我的表现，因为在更有动力却依然无法完成的情况下，会让人感到无比沮丧。

sentences.en: You could offer me the biggest incentive in the world or tell me that I've got the biggest consequence coming.
sentences.zh: 更不用说当你试图激励人们去做他们难以完成的事情时，你知道，

sentences.en: If I don't read it, it will not help.
sentences.zh: 你也在向他们传递一个不那么微妙的信息，即你认为他们不够努力。

sentences.en: And in fact, it'll decrease my performance because it'll be incredibly frustrating to be more motivated but still unable to do it.
sentences.zh: 否则你为什么要试图激励他们呢？

sentences.en: Not to mention that when you try to motivate people to do things that they struggle to do, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对于孩子，我可以告诉你，这已经给许多孩子的自尊心造成了巨大的伤害。

sentences.en: you also send them the not-so-subtle message that you don't think they're trying hard enough.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上，我认为当问题是某种身体问题时，更容易发现问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Or else why would you be trying to motivate them?
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，如果有人看不见黑板，你可以说，我可以带他们去看验光师，我可以给他们做个检查，我可以断定他们看不见黑板，

sentences.en: And, you know, with kids, I can tell you, that has caused so much damage to so many kids' self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 然后这就是解决方法，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, I think it's easier to see the problem when the problem is a physical problem of some kind, right?
sentences.zh: 但我认为部分原因是，你所谈论的一些技能更微妙，它们是心理层面的，不是直接可见的。

sentences.en: So, in other words, if someone can't see the board, you can say, I can take them to the optometrist, I can give them a test, I can tell that they can't see the board,
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到的只是结果，也就是那个孩子似乎没有在打扫房间。

sentences.en: and here's the fix, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But I think partly because some of these skills that you're talking about are subtler and they're psychological, they're not immediately visible.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And so all we see is the outcome, which is the kid doesn't seem to be cleaning his room.
sentences.zh: 然而，有趣的是，如果我们让100个在行为上有困难的人和100个没有困难的人排成一排，

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 然后我把他们带回我工作的麻省总医院精神科，给他们做神经心理学评估和测试，

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 就像验光师检查你的眼睛一样，猜猜你会看到什么？

sentences.en: And yet, the interesting thing is, if we line up 100 people who struggle with their behavior and 100 people who don't,
sentences.zh: 你会发现那些在行为上有困难的人在技能上存在巨大差异，我们现在正开始涵盖这些内容。

sentences.en: and I brought them back to our Department of Psychiatry here at Mass General Hospital, where I work, and gave them all neuropsychological evaluations, tests,
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特，你研究的另一个领域是情绪调节。

sentences.en: just like an optometrist might test your eyes, guess what you'll see?
sentences.zh: 谈谈这项技能。

sentences.en: You'll see the people who struggle with their behavior have huge differences in skills, and we're starting to cover those now.
sentences.zh: 所以，情绪调节，指的是我们控制或管理情绪的技能。

sentences.en: One of the other areas you've looked at, Stuart, is emotion regulation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，关于我们人类，我们知道的一件事是，感觉和思考之间存在一种负相关，即我们被感觉淹没得越多，

sentences.en: Talk about this skill.
sentences.zh: 我们思考得就越不清晰。

sentences.en: So, emotion regulation, that refers to our skills at controlling or managing our emotions.
sentences.zh: 感觉是好的。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the things we know about us humans is that there's sort of like a negative correlation between feeling and thinking, that the more we're flooded by feeling,
sentences.zh: 感觉告诉我们何时出现了需要解决的问题，但它往往不能解决问题。我们需要我们的思维技能。

sentences.en: the less clearly we are able to think.
sentences.zh: 因此，情绪调节技能是我们能够平息、管理或控制我们的情绪反应，以便我们能清晰思考的技能。

sentences.en: And feeling is good.
sentences.zh: 这可能是对挫折、愤怒、失望的情绪反应。

sentences.en: Feeling tells us when there's problems we need to solve, but it doesn't tend to solve probleMs. We need our thinking skills.
sentences.zh: 也可能是我们对兴奋、快乐、紧张、担忧等的情绪反应。

sentences.en: And so emotion regulation skills are our skills at being able to sort of tamp down or manage or control our emotional response so that we can think straight.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是技能。

sentences.en: And that may be emotional response to frustration, to anger, to disappointment.
sentences.zh: 谈谈属于社交领域的那类技能，即我们与他人的关系，我们与他人良好相处、良好协商的能力。

sentences.en: It could be our emotional response to excitement, to joy, nervousness, worry, etc.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这作为一种技能。

sentences.en: And those are skills.
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为我们许多人认为有些人就是有这种能力，有些人没有，有些人知道如何与他人相处，有些人不知道。

sentences.en: Talk about the category of skills that fall into the domain of the social, our relationships with others, our ability to deal well with others, to negotiate well with others.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特，谈谈这作为一种技能。

sentences.en: Talk about this as being a skill.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: Again, I think many of us assume some people just have it, some people don't have it, some people know how to get along with others, some people don't.
sentences.zh: 我真的把这些称为社交思维技能。

sentences.en: Talk about this as a skill, Stuart.
sentences.zh: 这些涵盖了从对某些人来说似乎非常基础的事情，比如你如何与某人开启一段对话？

sentences.en: Yes, sure.
sentences.zh: 或者你看到一群人正在做某事，你想加入他们。

sentences.en: And I refer to these as social thinking skills, really.
sentences.zh: 你如何在不破坏气氛的情况下加入那个群体？

sentences.en: And these are everything from like things that seem really basic for some people, like how do you start a conversation with somebody?
sentences.zh: 到更复杂的技能，比如你如何知道自己给人的印象如何，或者你的行为如何影响他人？

sentences.en: Or you see a group of people that you want to join doing something.
sentences.zh: 我称之为你的反馈循环，因为，你知道，我们都非常依赖它。

sentences.en: How do you join that group without sort of upsetting the apple cart?
sentences.zh: 我们都会做一些事情，然后扫描并观察效果如何，并相应地改变我们的行为。

sentences.en: To more complicated skills like how do you know how you're coming across or how your behavior is impacting somebody else?
sentences.zh: 但我曾与许多反馈循环受损的人共事。

sentences.en: I call it your feedback loop because, you know, we're all hugely dependent on it.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎无法从环境中获得反馈。

sentences.en: We all do things and we scan and we see how did that go across and we sort of change our behavior accordingly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会继续做一些让别人感到烦恼或反感的事情。

sentences.en: But I've worked with lots of people who have a broken feedback loop.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我会说一些最复杂的社交思维技能是诸如换位思考、设身处地为他人着想以及同理心之类的事情。

sentences.en: They sort of don't get the feedback from the environment.
sentences.zh: 同理心可能是最复杂的社交思维技能。

sentences.en: So they might keep doing something that's annoying to other people or off-putting.
sentences.zh: 所以你的核心理念之一是，人们如果能做好就能做好，而不是如果他们想做好就能做好。

sentences.en: And, you know, I would say some of the most complicated social thinking skills are things like perspective taking, putting yourself in somebody else's shoes, and empathy.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这种区别。

sentences.en: Empathy may be the most complicated social thinking skill.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So one of your central ideas is that people do well if they can do well, not if they want to do well.
sentences.zh: 这是我们工作背后的核心基础理念。

sentences.en: Talk about this distinction.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这种区别。

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: This is sort of the core foundational idea behind our work.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是我们工作背后的核心基础理念。

sentences.en: The notion, the philosophy that we taught, which we still teach today, is kids do well if they can.
sentences.zh: 我们所教导的，也是至今仍在传授的理念和哲学是：如果孩子们能做到，他们就会表现良好。

sentences.en: Applied to adults, adults do well if they can.
sentences.zh: 应用到成年人身上，如果成年人能做到，他们也会表现良好。

sentences.en: In other words, people do well if they can.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果人们能做到，他们就会表现良好。

sentences.en: What people do well if they can suggest is, you know what?
sentences.zh: “如果能做到就会表现良好”这一说法暗示了什么呢？你知道吗？

sentences.en: Don't we all want to do well?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不都想表现良好吗？

sentences.en: Like, show me the person who prefers doing poorly in the world.
sentences.zh: 比如，给我找出一个在这个世界上更愿意表现糟糕的人。

sentences.en: I've never met that person who prefers that things are going poorly at work,
sentences.zh: 我从未见过那种更愿意在工作中表现糟糕的人，

sentences.en: who prefers their partner is upset with them, who prefers that their parents are constantly, or teachers are upset.
sentences.zh: 也从未见过那种更愿意让伴侣对自己不满，或者更愿意让父母或老师不断对自己感到失望的人。

sentences.en: No, people do well if they can.
sentences.zh: 不，如果人们能做到，他们就会表现良好。

sentences.en: If they can, they will.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能做到，他们就会去做。

sentences.en: Now, that's a stark contrast to the notion of people do well if they want to.
sentences.zh: 这与“如果人们想做，他们就会表现良好”的观念形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Because what people do well if they want to suggests is, if they're not doing well, it must be because they don't want to.
sentences.zh: 因为“如果人们想做就会表现良好”所暗示的是：如果他们表现不好，那一定是因为他们不想。

sentences.en: What we need to do is make them want to.
sentences.zh: 我们需要做的是让他们产生意愿。

sentences.en: And, you know, if it only were as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果事情真有那么简单就好了。

sentences.en: My thought is, people do well if they can.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，如果人们能做到，他们就会表现良好。

sentences.en: If they could, they would.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能做到，他们就会去做。

sentences.en: And if they're not, let's use what we've learned in the last 50 years in terms of what might be getting in their way.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没做到，让我们利用过去50年学到的知识，看看是什么阻碍了他们。

sentences.en: One of the things that I'm taking away from our conversation, Stuart, is that it's possible that there might be situations where, in fact, people, you know, can do something,
sentences.zh: Stuart，从我们的谈话中我领悟到的一点是，确实可能存在这样一些情况：人们其实可以做某事，

sentences.en: but they don't want to do something.
sentences.zh: 但他们不想做。

sentences.en: It's possible that, in some ways, it's a problem of will.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这确实可能是一个意愿问题。

sentences.en: But I think the problem that arises when we assume that it's a problem of will as opposed to a problem of skill is it deprives us of our ability to do anything to help them.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，当我们将其归结为意愿问题而非技能问题时，问题在于这剥夺了我们帮助他们的能力。

sentences.en: As you're talking and as you're describing these various skills,
sentences.zh: 当你谈论并描述这些各种各样的技能时，

sentences.en: I'm thinking about various issues and various relationships that I have and people whom I know and things that I would like to see change.
sentences.zh: 我正在思考我所经历的各种问题和关系，以及我认识的人，还有我希望看到改变的事情。

sentences.en: And suddenly I'm thinking about them differently.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我开始以不同的方式看待他们了。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about them as saying, you know,
sentences.zh: 我开始这样想，你知道，

sentences.en: what if I could help this person develop this skill as opposed to what if I could just get into this person's thick skull what they need to be doing?
sentences.zh: 如果我能帮助这个人培养这项技能会怎样？而不是想，我该怎么才能把他们需要做的事情强塞进这个人的榆木脑袋里？

sentences.en: It's a very different mindset.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常不同的心态。

sentences.en: It's a huge shift in thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是一种思维上的巨大转变。

sentences.en: And what it does, as you're articulating beautifully, is it positions you in a much more empathic, understanding place.
sentences.zh: 正如你精彩阐述的那样，这样做让你处于一个更具同理心、更具理解力的位置。

sentences.en: And empathy is the bedrock of being able to help anyone.
sentences.zh: 而同理心是能够帮助任何人的基石。

sentences.en: So, you know, instead of blaming and wanting to control, it puts you in a solid place of nonjudgmental empathy, acceptance, and interest in what's going on for this person.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，与其责备和想要控制，不如让你处于一个坚实的、不带评判的同理心、接纳和关注对方处境的位置。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to inspire change by focusing on skill building instead of battles of will, not just in children, but in grownups too.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨如何通过专注于技能培养而非意愿之争来激发改变，这不仅适用于孩子，也适用于成年人。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedant.
sentences.zh: 我是 Shankar Vedant。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedant.
sentences.zh: 我是 Shankar Vedant。

sentences.en: When we encounter bad behavior, our instinct is often to discipline the behavior.
sentences.zh: 当我们遇到不良行为时，我们的本能往往是去惩戒这种行为。

sentences.en: We try to impose our will using rewards and consequences to force the behavior change.
sentences.zh: 我们试图通过奖励和后果来强加我们的意愿，以迫使行为改变。

sentences.en: Sometimes this works.
sentences.zh: 有时这很有效。

sentences.en: Sometimes it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 有时则不然。

sentences.en: Psychologist Stuart Ablon is the author of the book, Changeable, How Collaborative Problem Solving Changes Lives at Home.
sentences.zh: 心理学家 Stuart Ablon 是《Changeable: How Collaborative Problem Solving Changes Lives at Home》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Stuart, you say the standard approach we use to change people's behavior is something you call Plan A.
sentences.zh: Stuart，你说我们用来改变他人行为的标准方法是你所说的“A计划”。

sentences.en: Define Plan A for me.
sentences.zh: 请为我定义一下“A计划”。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Plan A is basically when you try to impose your will to make somebody do what you want them to do.
sentences.zh: “A计划”基本上就是当你试图强加自己的意愿，让某人做你想让他们做的事情时。

sentences.en: So, you know, whether it's harshly, gently, anything in between, if you're really just trying to make that person do what you want them to do, we call that Plan A.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，无论是严厉地、温和地，还是介于两者之间，如果你真的只是想让那个人做你想让他们做的事，我们就称之为“A计划”。

sentences.en: So, Plan A sounds pretty good on paper.
sentences.zh: 所以，“A计划”在理论上听起来很不错。

sentences.en: I mean, if you can actually get someone to change their behavior and this behavior is irritating, what's the downside?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你真的能让某人改变他们的行为，而这种行为又很令人恼火，那有什么坏处呢？

sentences.en: But it's fascinating because whether you're talking to a preschool teacher, a correctional facility guard, a police officer, someone in the corporate world, you name it.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，无论你是和幼儿园老师、惩教所警卫、警察，还是企业界的人士交谈，随便谁都行。

sentences.en: People always say the same thing, which is that trying to impose your will is an attempt to get your expectations met, but often isn't successful, often escalates poor behavior,
sentences.zh: 人们总是说同样的话，那就是试图强加意愿是试图满足你的期望，但往往并不成功，反而经常导致不良行为升级，

sentences.en: doesn't actually build any rapport or relationship, and the problem tends to live on.
sentences.zh: 实际上并没有建立任何融洽关系，而问题往往依然存在。

sentences.en: Also, if this is a person struggling with any skills, those skills don't get practiced or built when you try to impose your will as well.
sentences.zh: 此外，如果这是一个在某些技能上挣扎的人，当你试图强加意愿时，这些技能也得不到练习或培养。

sentences.en: So, before we get to Plan B, I want to shake things up a little bit and have you tell me what Plan C is in this rubric that you've created, Stuart.
sentences.zh: 所以，在进入“B计划”之前，我想稍微转换一下话题，让你告诉我你所创建的这个体系中的“C计划”是什么，Stuart。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Plan C is when you decide to drop your expectation or to solve the problem the way the other person wants it solved, which, very important clarification here,
sentences.zh: “C计划”是指你决定放弃你的期望，或者按照对方想要的方式解决问题，这里有一个非常重要的澄清，

sentences.en: is not, quote, giving in, because that's what people fear it is.
sentences.zh: 这并不是所谓的“屈服”，因为人们担心的正是这一点。

sentences.en: It's not giving in.
sentences.zh: 这不是屈服。

sentences.en: Giving in is when you try Plan A.
sentences.zh: 屈服是指当你尝试“A计划”时。

sentences.en: You try to impose your will and you can't pull it off and you bail and you sort of just give up.
sentences.zh: 你试图强加你的意愿，但你做不到，于是你退缩了，或者说你放弃了。

sentences.en: That's not Plan C.
sentences.zh: 那不是“C计划”。

sentences.en: That's failed Plan A leading to bailing.
sentences.zh: 那是失败的“A计划”导致了退缩。

sentences.en: Plan C is when you are planful.
sentences.zh: “C计划”是指你有计划地进行。

sentences.en: It's a strategic decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个战略性的决定。

sentences.en: You are deciding, I'm not going to pursue this, at least right now.
sentences.zh: 你决定：我暂时不追求这个目标，至少现在不。

sentences.en: Maybe not, this is not forever, just for now I'm not going to, or I'm going to solve it for now the way the other person wants it solved.
sentences.zh: 也许不是永远，只是现在我不打算这样做，或者我现在就按对方想要的方式把它解决掉。

sentences.en: And the reason you might do that is to keep the calm.
sentences.zh: 你这样做的原因是为了保持平静。

sentences.en: Plan C can decrease challenging behavior.
sentences.zh: “C计划”可以减少挑战性行为。

sentences.en: If you drop an expectation that leads to challenging behavior, you're going to get less challenging behavior.
sentences.zh: 如果你放弃了一个导致挑战性行为的期望，你就会得到较少的挑战性行为。

sentences.en: Now, you haven't solved the problem.
sentences.zh: 现在，你还没有解决问题。

sentences.en: You haven't gotten your expectations met, but you've avoided a challenge, for instance.
sentences.zh: 你还没有满足你的期望，但你避免了一场冲突，举例来说。

sentences.en: And there's a place for that.
sentences.zh: 而这也有其存在的意义。

sentences.en: Is there a better way than either Plan A or Plan C?
sentences.zh: 有没有比“A计划”或“C计划”更好的方法？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: And here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键在于这一点。

sentences.en: People so often get stuck, whether it's in a home, a school, a workplace, in what I call the A-C split.
sentences.zh: 人们经常陷入我所说的“A-C分裂”中，无论是在家庭、学校还是工作场所。

sentences.en: In a two-parent household, for instance, the A-C split is one parent's the Plan A parent, one parent's the Plan C parent.
sentences.zh: 例如，在双亲家庭中，“A-C分裂”就是一位家长是“A计划”型，另一位是“C计划”型。

sentences.en: But this happens in workplaces as well.
sentences.zh: 但这在工作场所也会发生。

sentences.en: And what I like to say is you don't get Plan B by the average of A and C.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你无法通过A和C的平均值得到“B计划”。

sentences.en: And there is another option, and that's Plan B.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个选择，那就是“B计划”。

sentences.en: Plan B is collaborative problem solving.
sentences.zh: “B计划”是协作式问题解决。

sentences.en: It is working together to solve a problem in mutually satisfactory ways.
sentences.zh: 它是共同努力，以双方都满意的方式解决问题。

sentences.en: And it has a clear set of guideposts to it that have been refined over years of practice and study at this point.
sentences.zh: 它有一套清晰的指导原则，这些原则在这一点上已经经过了多年的实践和研究的提炼。

sentences.en: What are these guideposts to it?
sentences.zh: 这些指导原则是什么？

sentences.en: Basically, there's three steps, or I prefer to call them ingredients, okay?
sentences.zh: 基本上有三个步骤，或者我更喜欢称之为要素，好吗？

sentences.en: And just to be clear at the outset, you can't use Plan B on someone.
sentences.zh: 首先要明确一点，你不能对某人“使用”B计划。

sentences.en: This is a process that you do with someone.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你与某人共同完成的过程。

sentences.en: But it has clear guideposts, and feel free to share those guideposts with the person that you are doing this with.
sentences.zh: 但它有清晰的指导原则，请随意与你正在进行此过程的人分享这些原则。

sentences.en: There's nothing hidden about this.
sentences.zh: 这没有什么可隐瞒的。

sentences.en: This is transparent.
sentences.zh: 这是透明的。

sentences.en: So the guideposts, these three ingredients are, first ingredient, the empathy ingredient.
sentences.zh: 所以这些指导原则，这三个要素，第一个要素是同理心要素。

sentences.en: And that is where you try to understand the other person's concern, perspective, point of view, or what's hard about a situation.
sentences.zh: 那就是你试图理解对方的顾虑、视角、观点，或者了解情况的难点所在。

sentences.en: And only once you've done that, that first ingredient, the empathy ingredient, do you move to the second ingredient, where you get to share your concern, your perspective,
sentences.zh: 只有当你完成了第一步，即同理心要素之后，你才能进入第二个要素，在那里你可以分享你的顾虑、你的视角、

sentences.en: your point of view, or what you're worried about.
sentences.zh: 你的观点，或者你担心的事情。

sentences.en: And only once you have two sets of concerns on the table do you go to the third ingredient, where you invite that person to work together,
sentences.zh: 只有当双方的顾虑都摆在桌面上时，你才能进入第三个要素，邀请对方共同努力，

sentences.en: to collaborate with you to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 与你协作解决问题。

sentences.en: You must have both parties' concerns on the table.
sentences.zh: 你必须把双方的顾虑都摆在桌面上。

sentences.en: Just to drill down a little bit deeper into each of these three steps, I think when we genuinely ask someone what their problem is,
sentences.zh: 为了深入探讨这三个步骤中的每一个，我认为当我们真诚地问某人他们的问题是什么时，

sentences.en: and you did that with the kid who was basically shutting you off at the pass and saying, I don't know, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 你对那个基本上把你拒之门外，说“我不知道，我不在乎”的孩子就是这样做的。

sentences.en: When you genuinely ask that question, I think there's an element of courage that's required when you do this.
sentences.zh: 当你真诚地提出这个问题时，我认为这样做需要一种勇气。

sentences.en: Because I think very often, I'm not sure we actually want to know what's preventing someone from doing the thing that we want them to do.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为很多时候，我不确定我们是否真的想知道是什么阻碍了某人去做我们想让他们做的事情。

sentences.en: We don't want to know that there's a genuine problem, a genuine roadblock.
sentences.zh: 我们不想知道存在一个真正的问题，一个真正的障碍。

sentences.en: And what you're saying is that that empathy is actually really an important first step.
sentences.zh: 而你所说的是，那种同理心实际上确实是非常重要的第一步。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And there's a stance, okay?
sentences.zh: 而且这是一种立场，好吗？

sentences.en: You know, when people hear the word empathy, by the way, they often misunderstand it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，顺便说一句，当人们听到“同理心”这个词时，他们经常误解它。

sentences.en: They think empathy means to sort of show you care, and that you can empathize by saying, you know, I really want to work this out with you.
sentences.zh: 他们认为同理心意味着表现出你在乎，你可以通过说“你知道，我真的很想和你一起解决这个问题”来表达同理心。

sentences.en: Like, that's empathy.
sentences.zh: 就像，那就是同理心。

sentences.en: That's not empathy.
sentences.zh: 那不是同理心。

sentences.en: If anything, it's like drive-by empathy.
sentences.zh: 如果非要说的话，那就像是“快餐式同理心”。

sentences.en: But real empathy, the definition of the word empathy, is to understand.
sentences.zh: 但真正的同理心，同理心这个词的定义，是理解。

sentences.en: And you have to work hard to try to understand somebody else's point of view and perspective.
sentences.zh: 你必须努力去尝试理解别人的观点和视角。

sentences.en: And you're right, that sometimes we may not like what we're going to hear.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，有时我们可能不喜欢我们将要听到的内容。

sentences.en: And there's a really important lesson in here, which is I'm constantly trying to remind myself and others that empathy doesn't mean to agree or to disagree.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个非常重要的教训，那就是我不断地提醒自己和他人，同理心并不意味着同意或不同意。

sentences.en: Empathy is not agreeing or disagreeing.
sentences.zh: 同理心不是同意或不同意。

sentences.en: It is simply understanding.
sentences.zh: 它仅仅是理解。

sentences.en: And actually, believe it or not, you can completely and totally disagree with somebody's perspective and point of view, and you can still empathize by understanding.
sentences.zh: 事实上，信不信由你，你可以完全不同意某人的视角和观点，但你仍然可以通过理解来产生同理心。

sentences.en: And frankly, I think this has become something that we've gotten worse and worse at, which is when you don't agree with somebody, can you still understand and listen to them?
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我认为这已经成为我们越来越不擅长的事情，那就是当你不同意某人时，你还能理解并倾听他们吗？

sentences.en: Let's just drill down a moment into that first point that you're making, Stuart, the idea of being empathetic and curious.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨一下你提到的第一点，Stuart，即保持同理心和好奇心的想法。

sentences.en: You say that even here, there are actually multiple elements to this prong.
sentences.zh: 你说即使在这里，这个要素实际上也有多个组成部分。

sentences.en: What do they involve?
sentences.zh: 它们涉及什么？

sentences.en: Well, so, you know, as I mentioned, empathy is hard.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我提到的，同理心很难。

sentences.en: It's not what people think it is.
sentences.zh: 它不是人们所想的那样。

sentences.en: Empathy is understanding, and it's really hard for people to do.
sentences.zh: 同理心是理解，这对人们来说真的很难做到。

sentences.en: And I've had the opportunity to watch so many people in so many different places try to do collaborative problem solving, and the first ingredient is the hardeSt.
sentences.zh: 我有机会观察了许多人在许多不同地方尝试进行协作式问题解决，而第一个要素是最难的。

sentences.en: And so what I did is I actually started to take all these recordings, audio, video recordings,
sentences.zh: 所以我所做的是，我实际上开始收集所有这些录音、音频、视频录像，

sentences.en: of all these attempts that people made at doing collaborative problem solving and just studying the first ingredient.
sentences.zh: 记录人们在进行协作式问题解决时的所有尝试，并专门研究第一个要素。

sentences.en: And, of course, my own attempts as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，也包括我自己的尝试。

sentences.en: And what I found is fascinating, that when it goes well, when we're doing a good job empathizing, we're doing four things and four things only.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一个迷人的事实：当进展顺利时，当我们做得很好时，我们只做了四件事，而且仅仅是这四件事。

sentences.en: These four things are, like any good detective would, asking a lot of questions, clarifying questions.
sentences.zh: 这四件事是：像任何优秀的侦探一样，提出大量的问题，澄清性的问题。

sentences.en: If you're not getting information, educated guessing, that's the second thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有得到信息，就进行有根据的猜测，这是第二件事。

sentences.en: If you get any information, either in response to your question or in response to an educated guess, you reflect back in your own words what you've heard from the person.
sentences.zh: 如果你得到了任何信息，无论是对你问题的回应还是对有根据猜测的回应，你都要用自己的话复述你从对方那里听到的内容。

sentences.en: We call that reflective listening.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“反思性倾听”。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: And that shows you're listening.
sentences.zh: 这表明你在倾听。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: And the fourth thing is reassurance.
sentences.zh: 第四件事是安抚。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: And what reassurance is, is your way of saying this is not some tricky form of plan A.
sentences.zh: 安抚是你表达“这不是A计划的某种诡计”的方式。

sentences.en: So it's you saying things like, don't worry, you're not in trouble.
sentences.zh: 所以你是在说这样的话：别担心，你没有麻烦。

sentences.en: Or I'm just trying to understand.
sentences.zh: 或者“我只是想了解一下”。

sentences.en: Or one of my personal favorites.
sentences.zh: 或者我个人最喜欢的一句。

sentences.en: I know there must be an important reason that.
sentences.zh: “我知道一定有一个重要的原因，导致……”

sentences.en: Fill in the blank.
sentences.zh: 填空。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: Because what I always remind myself is I may not love the person's behavior, but I'm sure they've got a good reason, a good concern, a good perspective.
sentences.zh: 因为我总是提醒自己，我可能不喜欢这个人的行为，但我相信他们一定有一个很好的理由，一个很好的顾虑，一个很好的视角。

sentences.en: That's what you're on the hunt for.
sentences.zh: 这就是你要寻找的东西。

sentences.en: And the last thing I would say about this is your stance should be one of curiosity.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我想说的最后一件事是，你的立场应该是好奇。

sentences.en: It is way too easy to enter a conversation with preconceived notions and judgments.
sentences.zh: 带着先入为主的观念和判断进入对话太容易了。

sentences.en: Suspend those.
sentences.zh: 暂停这些念头。

sentences.en: Ask questions.
sentences.zh: 提出问题。

sentences.en: Take guesses.
sentences.zh: 试着猜猜看。

sentences.en: Reflect what you've heard.
sentences.zh: 复述你所听到的内容。

sentences.en: Reassure if necessary.
sentences.zh: 必要时给予安抚。

sentences.en: And you'll learn a lot.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能学到很多。

sentences.en: So the second step that you suggested a second ago is that once you've done the necessary empathizing, you've tried to understand where the other person is coming from,
sentences.zh: 那么你刚才提到的第二步是，一旦你完成了必要的共情，尝试理解了对方的立场，

sentences.en: you put your own perspective on the table.
sentences.zh: 你就摆出自己的观点。

sentences.en: But I can see how this might backfire, Stuart.
sentences.zh: 但我能看出这可能会适得其反，斯图尔特。

sentences.en: I listen to you very carefully.
sentences.zh: 我会非常认真地倾听你。

sentences.en: I'm patient.
sentences.zh: 我很有耐心。

sentences.en: I'm genuinely curious.
sentences.zh: 我真心感到好奇。

sentences.en: I try and understand where you're coming from.
sentences.zh: 我试着去理解你的立场。

sentences.en: And once I've understood it, I say, all right, that's all well and good, but here's what I think.
sentences.zh: 一旦我理解了，我会说，好吧，这些都很好，但这是我的想法。

sentences.en: Could that be a problem?
sentences.zh: 这会有问题吗？

sentences.en: It could be a problem.
sentences.zh: 这可能会有问题。

sentences.en: And the first thing I'm going to suggest is a little tweak in wording, not that there's magic words out there.
sentences.zh: 我首先要建议的是对措辞做一点微调，并不是说有什么灵丹妙药。

sentences.en: But the word but almost sort of implies, okay, I heard you, but guess what?
sentences.zh: 但“但是”这个词几乎暗示着，好吧，我听到了，但你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: My perspective is different or more important than yours.
sentences.zh: 我的观点与你不同，或者比你的更重要。

sentences.en: I always encourage people to say, you know, once you've heard the other person out, first of all,
sentences.zh: 我总是鼓励人们，你知道，一旦你听完了对方的话，首先，

sentences.en: summarize what you've heard from them so that you really are showing you've heard it.
sentences.zh: 总结一下你从他们那里听到的内容，这样你才能真正表明你听进去了。

sentences.en: And then use the word and instead.
sentences.zh: 然后改用“而且”这个词。

sentences.en: And just say and, you know, here's my point of view or here's my concern or my perspective.
sentences.zh: 直接说“而且”，你知道，这是我的观点，或者这是我的顾虑或看法。

sentences.en: Now, what you're saying is the person might get upset with that or sort of, you know, it might go off the rails a little bit.
sentences.zh: 现在，你说的是对方可能会因此感到不安，或者，你知道，事情可能会有点失控。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And guess what that would tell you?
sentences.zh: 你猜这说明了什么？

sentences.en: That this person may have some difficulty with perspective taking or emotion regulation skills.
sentences.zh: 说明这个人可能在换位思考或情绪调节能力方面有一些困难。

sentences.en: Or they may have just had a lot of plan A interactions and assume that right after you've heard them, here comes plan A.
sentences.zh: 或者他们只是经历过太多“A计划”式的互动，认为你听完他们的话后，紧接着就要实施“A计划”了。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's not magic.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这并不是什么魔法。

sentences.en: It's going to take some repetition.
sentences.zh: 这需要一些重复练习。

sentences.en: Again, collaborative problem solving has three big steps.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，协作式问题解决有三大重要步骤。

sentences.en: First, empathize with the other party's concerns.
sentences.zh: 第一，对另一方的顾虑表示共情。

sentences.en: Once you've understood where they're coming from and they agree you have understood their point of view, you say, and here's my perspective.
sentences.zh: 一旦你理解了他们的立场，并且他们也同意你理解了他们的观点，你就说，这是我的看法。

sentences.en: Here are my concerns.
sentences.zh: 这是我的顾虑。

sentences.en: When it comes to the third step, which is coming up with a collaborative solution, Stuart says it's important not to make the first move.
sentences.zh: 说到第三步，也就是共同提出协作解决方案，斯图尔特说不要先发制人很重要。

sentences.en: Once you've clarified the problem to solve, which is once you've identified the respective concerns, there's a lot of reasons.
sentences.zh: 一旦你明确了要解决的问题，也就是确定了双方各自的顾虑，原因有很多。

sentences.en: You want to invite the other person to take first crack at solutions.
sentences.zh: 你想邀请对方先尝试提出解决方案。

sentences.en: First of all, when you invite that person to come up with an idea, you are giving them ownership, autonomy.
sentences.zh: 首先，当你邀请对方提出想法时，你是在赋予他们所有权和自主权。

sentences.en: You know, they're co-author of a solution as opposed to you sort of, even if you're trying to do it in the best of collaborative spirits,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是解决方案的共同作者，而不是你，即使你是本着最好的协作精神去做的，

sentences.en: if you're the one suggesting the first solution, it might feel imposed upon them.
sentences.zh: 如果你是那个提出第一个解决方案的人，对方可能会觉得这是强加给他们的。

sentences.en: And if they're co-authored, they're going to be much more invested in that.
sentences.zh: 如果他们是共同作者，他们会投入更多。

sentences.en: But beyond that, you know, this is an opportunity to actually get a chance to see how that person does,
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，你知道，这是一个机会，可以让你真正看看那个人的表现如何，

sentences.en: what their skills are like coming up with a solution that is theoretically mutually satisfactory, realistic and doable.
sentences.zh: 看看他们在提出理论上双方满意、现实且可行的解决方案方面的能力如何。

sentences.en: I work with lots of people who they'll come up with a solution, but it's not mutually satisfactory or it's not realistic or it's not doable.
sentences.zh: 我和很多人共事过，他们会提出解决方案，但那并不让双方满意，或者不现实，或者不可行。

sentences.en: And so they need practice.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要练习。

sentences.en: Well, guess how you're going to practice and develop that skill?
sentences.zh: 那么，猜猜你将如何练习并发展这项技能？

sentences.en: Not by watching somebody else solve probleMs.
sentences.zh: 不是通过看别人解决问题。

sentences.en: I mean, when you teach a kid to ride a bike, do you hop on the bike and say, all right, watch me ride.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你教孩子骑自行车时，你会跳上车说，好吧，看我骑。

sentences.en: You got it?
sentences.zh: 学会了吗？

sentences.en: Here you go.
sentences.zh: 给你。

sentences.en: You should be good now.
sentences.zh: 你现在应该没问题了。

sentences.en: No, watching someone else come up with ideas doesn't help somebody practice and develop problem-solving skills.
sentences.zh: 不，看别人想出点子并不能帮助某人练习和发展解决问题的能力。

sentences.en: I think some people might hear this approach, Stuart, and say, all right,
sentences.zh: 我想有些人听到这种方法可能会说，好吧，斯图尔特，

sentences.en: this is actually perhaps a clever way into manipulating this other person to doing what I really want them to do.
sentences.zh: 这其实可能是一种巧妙的方法，用来操纵对方去做我真正想让他们做的事。

sentences.en: So I listen to them very carefully.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常认真地听他们说。

sentences.en: I offer them my perspective.
sentences.zh: 我向他们提供我的观点。

sentences.en: I let them come up with the idea.
sentences.zh: 我让他们自己想出点子。

sentences.en: And all the while, I'm trying to keep in mind what it is that I finally want, the outcome that I finally want, and try and push and nudge to get to that outcome.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，我一直记着我最终想要什么，我最终想要的成果，并试图推动和引导以达到那个成果。

sentences.en: It's just sort of a sneaky psychological way of getting to what I want in the first place.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种狡猾的心理手段，用来达到我最初想要的目的。

sentences.en: I think you're actually suggesting something different, that, in fact,
sentences.zh: 我认为你实际上是在建议一些不同的东西，事实上，

sentences.en: collaborative problem-solving is not just a backdoor way into manipulating someone to get what you want all along.
sentences.zh: 协作式问题解决不仅仅是操纵他人以达到你一直想要的目的的后门途径。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: In fact, I would call that tricky plan A, not plan B, because a really important distinction here is you actually shouldn't know what the solution is going to be.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我会称之为“狡猾的A计划”，而不是B计划，因为这里一个非常重要的区别是，你实际上不应该预设解决方案会是什么。

sentences.en: If you already know what the solution is and you're just trying to get the person there, yeah, that's plan A.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经知道解决方案是什么，并且只是想让对方达到那个结果，是的，那就是A计划。

sentences.en: That's just a tricky form of plan A.
sentences.zh: 那只是A计划的一种狡猾形式。

sentences.en: Now, what you need to do is you need to think of what is your concern?
sentences.zh: 现在，你需要做的是思考你的顾虑是什么？

sentences.en: What are you worried about?
sentences.zh: 你在担心什么？

sentences.en: What's your point of view?
sentences.zh: 你的观点是什么？

sentences.en: What is wanting you to come up with that solution?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你想要提出那个解决方案？

sentences.en: What are you worried about?
sentences.zh: 你在担心什么？

sentences.en: And you hold on tight to that.
sentences.zh: 你要紧紧抓住这一点。

sentences.en: You don't relinquish that.
sentences.zh: 不要放弃它。

sentences.en: And the solution has to address your concern.
sentences.zh: 解决方案必须解决你的顾虑。

sentences.en: But it also has to address the other party's concern.
sentences.zh: 但它也必须解决对方的顾虑。

sentences.en: That's the difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是区别。

sentences.en: That's collaborative problem-solving.
sentences.zh: 这就是协作式问题解决。

sentences.en: And, of course, partly what all of this is pointing to, Stuart, is humility.
sentences.zh: 当然，斯图尔特，这一切所指向的部分原因在于谦逊。

sentences.en: Because I think very often, I think when we're trying to change someone, we are so confident that we know why they're not doing what they should be doing.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为很多时候，当我们试图改变某人时，我们非常自信地认为我们知道他们为什么不做他们应该做的事。

sentences.en: We're so confident that we know what they should be doing and how they should be doing it that one reason we don't stop to actually ask, well, what's going on in your head?
sentences.zh: 我们非常自信地认为我们知道他们应该做什么以及应该怎么做，所以我们不停止下来去真正问问，好吧，你脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: What could be happening in your mind is that we don't have the humility to accept that, in fact, we might not have all the answers ourselves.
sentences.zh: 你脑子里可能在发生什么，原因是我们没有谦逊去接受，事实上，我们自己可能并没有所有的答案。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when we can suspend those assumptions and be really curious, we learn so much.
sentences.zh: 当我们能放下那些假设并真正保持好奇时，我们会学到很多。

sentences.en: And not only do we learn so much, but it really connects us to people.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅学到了很多，而且它真正地将我们与他人连接起来。

sentences.en: People ask me that all the time.
sentences.zh: 人们总是问我这个问题。

sentences.en: They say, how do you really get somebody to listen to you?
sentences.zh: 他们说，你如何真正让别人听你的？

sentences.en: And I say, by listening to them.
sentences.zh: 我说，通过倾听他们。

sentences.en: Listen to them really hard, really well, really effectively.
sentences.zh: 非常努力、非常好、非常有效地倾听他们。

sentences.en: And they'll be a whole lot more likely to listen to you.
sentences.zh: 他们会更有可能听你的。

sentences.en: When we come back, collaborative problem-solving in action.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将展示协作式问题解决的实际应用。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Whether it's an unruly child, a spouse who forgets important dates, or a co-worker who says inappropriate things at meetings,
sentences.zh: 无论是顽皮的孩子、忘记重要日期的配偶，还是在会议上说不恰当话语的同事，

sentences.en: it can be hard to get people to behave the way you want them to.
sentences.zh: 要让人们按照你想要的方式行事可能很困难。

sentences.en: Psychologist Stuart Ablon says the solution is collaborative problem-solving,
sentences.zh: 心理学家斯图尔特·阿布隆说，解决方案是协作式问题解决，

sentences.en: coming to mutually agreeable solutions together.
sentences.zh: 共同达成双方都能接受的解决方案。

sentences.en: One of the places he tested his ideas was a state psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 他测试自己想法的地方之一是一家州立精神病院。

sentences.en: It was infamous because it was the setting for a disturbing movie about the mistreatment of patients.
sentences.zh: 它臭名昭著，因为它是那部关于虐待病人的令人不安的电影的拍摄地。

sentences.en: I always tell people, the Oregon State Hospital, I ask people, do you know it?
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉人们，俄勒冈州立医院，我问人们，你知道它吗？

sentences.en: Everybody says no.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说不知道。

sentences.en: And I say, well, actually, you do.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，其实你知道。

sentences.en: Because it was featured in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's NeSt.
sentences.zh: 因为它在《飞越疯人院》中出现过。

sentences.en: Now, that original hospital has been torn down.
sentences.zh: 现在，那家原来的医院已经被拆除了。

sentences.en: There's a beautiful, big, hulking new hospital.
sentences.zh: 那里有一座漂亮、巨大、笨重的新医院。

sentences.en: But I have to tell you, from having spent some time there, the sort of traumas of the past almost echo through the walls there.
sentences.zh: 但我必须告诉你，在待过一段时间后，过去的创伤几乎在墙壁间回荡。

sentences.en: And we were contacted because staff were being assaulted at alarming rates and all kinds of injuries of their patients,
sentences.zh: 我们被联系是因为工作人员正以惊人的频率受到袭击，还有各种各样的病人受伤，

sentences.en: the clients there, and the staff as well.
sentences.zh: 那里的客户，以及工作人员也是如此。

sentences.en: I remember at one point,
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，

sentences.en: the staff had actually set up a Facebook page to post the pictures of their injuries to try to get people to pay attention to that something was really wrong here.
sentences.zh: 工作人员实际上建立了一个Facebook页面来发布他们受伤的照片，试图让人们注意到这里确实出了大问题。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And we were brought in to try to change that dynamic.
sentences.zh: 我们被请来试图改变那种动态。

sentences.en: So when you call this a hospital, you know, the image that I have is sort of doctors and nurses walking around and people holding charts.
sentences.zh: 所以当你称这为医院时，你知道，我脑海中的形象是医生和护士走来走去，人们拿着病历表。

sentences.en: That's not quite the right picture, is it, Stuart?
sentences.zh: 那不是正确的画面，对吧，斯图尔特？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: This is a state psychiatric hospital with over 1,000 patients.
sentences.zh: 这是一所拥有超过1000名病人的州立精神病院。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of them are guilty, if not for insanity.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数人是有罪的，如果不是因为精神错乱的话。

sentences.en: So they are there for having committed rather serious crimes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是因为犯下了相当严重的罪行才在那里。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's somewhere between what you might think of as a hospital, but probably closer to what a correctional facility looks like.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它介于你可能认为的医院之间，但可能更接近惩教设施的样子。

sentences.en: You know, you've got to be buzzed in and out of several doors to get in there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你必须经过几道门被蜂鸣器控制进出才能进去。

sentences.en: It's maximum security.
sentences.zh: 那是最高安全级别。

sentences.en: You know, the restrooms have a fixed toilet with nothing that could be ripped off and used as a weapon or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，洗手间里有固定的马桶，没有任何东西可以被拆下来当作武器或类似的东西。

sentences.en: It's a pretty tough place.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当艰难的地方。

sentences.en: So the hospital wanted to improve conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以医院想要改善条件。

sentences.en: I would have imagined that this would be a difficult place to think about collaborative problem solving.
sentences.zh: 我本以为这会是一个很难考虑协作式问题解决的地方。

sentences.en: Describe for me the work that you did and what you found.
sentences.zh: 请描述一下你所做的工作以及你的发现。

sentences.en: Well, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得对。

sentences.en: It is a difficult place, was a difficult place.
sentences.zh: 这是一个困难的地方，曾经是一个困难的地方。

sentences.en: But I have to say I found a decent amount of receptivity there from folks because, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，我在那里的人们身上发现了不少接受度，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: it's people who work in those situations that know firsthand that levying rewards and punishments really is not very effective and creates all kinds of hostility and makes for a pretty miserable job.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下工作的人亲身体会到，施加奖励和惩罚确实不太有效，而且会产生各种敌意，让工作变得非常痛苦。

sentences.en: So they were eager to learn something else.
sentences.zh: 所以他们渴望学习别的东西。

sentences.en: But I will also say skeptical and for good reason.
sentences.zh: 但我也会说，他们持怀疑态度，而且是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: And so it took a little while to really have people begin to shift their mindsets because you can't come right in and just teach people a new way of doing things.
sentences.zh: 所以花了一段时间才真正让人们开始转变思维方式，因为你不能直接走进去就教人们一种做事的新方法。

sentences.en: You first have to help them understand why would you do something differently in the first place.
sentences.zh: 你首先必须帮助他们理解为什么你首先要以不同的方式做事。

sentences.en: And that's that shift from it's not as simple as people do well if they want to.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种转变，从“如果人们想做，他们就能做好”这种简单的想法中转变出来。

sentences.en: We just got to make them want to.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要让他们想做。

sentences.en: It's people do well if they can.
sentences.zh: 而是“如果人们能做到，他们就能做好”。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of research that shows these people are here because they're struggling with a lack of skill, not a lack of will.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多研究表明，这些人在这里是因为他们缺乏技能，而不是缺乏意愿。

sentences.en: So you tell the story of one middle-aged patient who suffered from a history of schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 所以你讲了一个患有精神分裂症病史的中年病人的故事。

sentences.en: Tell me his story, Stuart.
sentences.zh: 告诉我他的故事，斯图尔特。

sentences.en: This was a man who had actually been refusing to attend any of the therapeutic elements of the program.
sentences.zh: 这是一个实际上一直拒绝参加该项目任何治疗环节的男人。

sentences.en: So they would, you know, the patients would stay in their cell blocks, but they would come down to what they called the treatment mall to have individual and group therapy.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会，你知道，病人们会待在他们的牢房区，但他们会来到他们所谓的治疗中心进行个人和团体治疗。

sentences.en: And this guy would refuse to come down there.
sentences.zh: 而这个人会拒绝下来。

sentences.en: Now, you can imagine what they would typically try.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以想象他们通常会尝试什么。

sentences.en: They would typically try some form of plan A to try to impose their will to get him down there, which is if you don't come, you will lose this privilege, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 他们通常会尝试某种形式的A计划，试图强加他们的意志让他下来，也就是如果你不来，你就会失去这个特权，等等。

sentences.en: If you do, you get these privileges.
sentences.zh: 如果你做了，你就会得到这些特权。

sentences.en: And believe it or not, the hospital itself was designed around these principles.
sentences.zh: 信不信由你，医院本身就是围绕这些原则设计的。

sentences.en: Even the building, the building has a store that was built where people could, you know, accrue rewards and things like that.
sentences.zh: 甚至那栋建筑，建筑里有一个商店，人们可以在那里，你知道，积累奖励之类的东西。

sentences.en: So they had tried this, and frankly, it got ugly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们尝试过这个，坦率地说，情况变得很糟糕。

sentences.en: There were several assaults trying to get this rather large man down to the treatment mall.
sentences.zh: 为了让这个相当高大的男人下到治疗中心，发生了好几次袭击事件。

sentences.en: And so what they started to do was plan C, which is say, you know what, it's just not worth all of this, so I guess he won't attend.

sentences.zh: 人们有一种误解，认为当你进行协作解决问题时，它有点

sentences.en: of means anything goes or you're not setting any limits or boundaries.

sentences.en: That's like a really lame way to hold somebody accountable.

sentences.en: And isn't ultimately the sort of most powerful way to hold somebody accountable and have them take responsibility for their actions,

sentences.zh: 它们就像使用奖励和后果来试图塑造行为的非常有组织的方式。

sentences.en: And what all that research has shown is it's not like rewards and consequences are bad and you should never use them, but they're good at some things and not good at other things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些研究表明，并不是说奖励和后果是坏的，你不应该使用它们，但它们在某些事情上是好的，而在其他事情上则不然。

sentences.zh: 它们善于提醒人们对他们的期望是什么，什么是对的，什么是错的。

sentences.en: And they're good at motivating people to do those things.

sentences.en: What are they not good at?

sentences.en: It's not their fault.

sentences.en: They just were never intended to be used that way.

sentences.en: They're not good at building a helping relationship between one person and another.

sentences.en: And ultimately, they're not good at helping people stay calm in the midst of frustration, as we talked about.
